title: Fixed-object rectification for enriched categories
statement:
Let $S$ be a set, and put $\mathbf V=\operatorname{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$ with the projective monoidal model structure of [lem-coef-projective-chains-monoidal-model]. Let $W$ be its weak equivalences, namely quasi-isomorphisms of unbounded cochain complexes, in the convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\operatorname{Cat}_S(\mathbf V)$ for the category of strict $\mathbf V$-enriched categories with object set exactly $S$ and enriched functors equal to the identity on $S$: their mapping complexes have associative unital chain-map compositions. Let $\mathrm{FF}_S$ be the functors inducing quasi-isomorphisms on every mapping complex. Write $\Delta_S^{\mathrm{op}}$ for the category of lists $(s_0,\ldots,s_n)$, with a map to $(s_{\phi(0)},\ldots,s_{\phi(m)})$ for each order-preserving $\phi:[m]\to[n]$; projection records $[n]$ in the opposite simplex category. Its categorical algebras in a monoidal infinity-category are the functors to its monoidal category of operators over the opposite simplex category carrying coCartesian arrows over inert maps to coCartesian arrows; an inert map $\phi:[m]\to[n]$ satisfies $\phi(i)=\phi(0)+i$ for all $i$. These algebras encode mapping objects indexed by $S\times S$ and coherently associative unital composition.

With $\mathbf D_\infty(\mathbf Z)=\mathbf V[W^{-1}]_\infty$, there is a natural equivalence
$$\eta_S:\operatorname{Cat}_S(\mathbf V)[\mathrm{FF}_S^{-1}]_\infty\simeq\operatorname{Alg}_{\Delta_S^{\mathrm{op}}}(\mathbf D_\infty(\mathbf Z)).$$
It is natural, with coherent compatibility, under restriction along functions of sets. The comparison is induced by applying monoidal localization to cofibrant enriched categories; their mapping complexes are cofibrant complexes. For an arbitrary enriched category choose a fixed-object cofibrant replacement $Q\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ in the objectwise quasi-isomorphism model structure. The resulting mapping object is naturally equivalent to the class of $\mathcal A(s,t)$ in $\mathbf D_\infty(\mathbf Z)$. Under this equivalence, the degree-zero cohomology class of a closed arrow is its underlying homotopy-category arrow. These identifications are natural for enriched functors after localization.

source.place: Definitions 2.8–2.9 and 5.1, Proposition 5.2, and Corollary 3.15 (cofibrant mapping objects); specialize using Example 5.11. Read online, not archived; no Stacks tag states this fixed-object operadic rectification.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal D=\mathbf D_\infty(\mathbf Z)$. The projective-chain theorem [lem-coef-projective-chains-monoidal-model] gives a presentably symmetric monoidal localization and a cofibrant tensor unit. Apply [lem-coef-fixed-object-dg-free-model] to the fixed small set $S$. We obtain $\mathcal C_S=\operatorname{Cat}_S(\mathbf V)[\mathrm{FF}_S^{-1}]_\infty$, its graph functor $U_\infty:\mathcal C_S\to\mathcal D^{S^2}$, the free adjunction $F_\infty\dashv U_\infty$, and the fixed-object functorial replacement $Q_S$. In particular $U_\infty$ is conservative and preserves geometric realizations. Applying [lem-coef-categorical-algebra-free-monad] to $\mathcal D$ supplies the other graph functor $V_S:\mathcal A_S\to\mathcal D^{S^2}$, its left adjoint $G_S$, conservativity, and geometric-realization preservation. Both source categories have these colimits: for $\mathcal C_S$ this follows from the combinatorial model and [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability], and $\mathcal A_S$ is presentable by the algebra theorem. Work in nested universes with $S$ small, as in [def-coef-complete-algebroid].

source.place: Proof of Proposition 5.2(a)-(e), with Lemma 3.20 and Example 5.11.

proof.text: For a locally cofibrant dg category $A$, apply monoidal localization to its cofibrant mapping complexes. On strings send $(s_0,\ldots,s_n)$ to $(L A(s_0,s_1),\ldots,L A(s_{n-1},s_n))$; inert maps select adjacent entries. The operator convention is forward order, whereas strict dg composition is reverse order. Define the binary active operation by $a\otimes b\mapsto(-1)^{|a||b|}ba$, and the operation on $n$ entries by signed reversal followed by iterated strict composition. Its sign is $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}|a_i||a_j|}$. For a partition into consecutive blocks, first reversing within blocks contributes the within-block pairs, and then reversing the blocks contributes the between-block pairs, because the degree of a block product is the sum of its degrees. The total exponent is exactly the displayed sum. Thus substitution of active operations agrees with the single iterated operation. The length-zero operation is the unit, whose degree is zero, so inserting units changes no sign. These formulas define the functor to the category of operators and its inert-preserving algebra structure in [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. The monoidal localization in [lem-coef-projective-chains-monoidal-model] retains these coherences, and tensors of these cofibrant complexes compute derived tensors. The construction is functorial for dg functors. A mappingwise quasi-isomorphism maps to an algebra equivalence by conservativity in [lem-coef-categorical-algebra-free-monad].

source.place: Definitions 2.8–2.9 and 5.1; explicit Koszul convention for the comparison.

proof.text: Let $\mathbf C_S^{\rm lc}$ be the full relative subcategory on locally cofibrant dg categories, with mappingwise quasi-isomorphisms. Its coherent localization exists by [lem-coef-simplicial-localization-existence]. The replacement $Q_S$ of [lem-coef-fixed-object-dg-free-model] takes all dg categories to cofibrant, hence locally cofibrant, ones. Naturality of $q:Q_S\to1$ and two-out-of-three imply that $Q_S$ preserves mappingwise quasi-isomorphisms. If $j$ is the inclusion of $\mathbf C_S^{\rm lc}$, then $q$ gives relative transformations $jQ_S\to1$ and $Q_Sj\to1$ whose components are weak equivalences. The map $\mathbf C_S^{\rm lc}\to L(\mathbf C_S^{\rm lc})$ exhibits a localization in the sense of [def-coef-universally-localizing-simplicial-map], and $\mathbf C_S\to\mathcal C_S$ is the homotopy coherent localization of the combinatorial model category of [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability]; in both cases precomposition is a functor equivalence from functors on the localization onto the full subcategory of functors inverting the weak equivalences. So $j$ and $Q_S$ descend, and the two transformations, viewed as edges of $\operatorname{Fun}(N(\mathbf C_S),\mathcal C_S)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(N(\mathbf C_S^{\rm lc}),L(\mathbf C_S^{\rm lc}))$ between functors inverting weak equivalences, descend to edges between the descended composites. Their components at objects of $\mathbf C_S$, resp. $\mathbf C_S^{\rm lc}$, are images of quasi-isomorphisms, hence equivalences, so by [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] they are equivalence edges of the functor categories on $N(\mathbf C_S)$ and $N(\mathbf C_S^{\rm lc})$; the inverse functor equivalence then makes the descended transformations equivalences. Thus $j$ becomes an equivalence with inverse $Q_S$. Descend Step 2 along this equivalence to obtain $\eta_S:\mathcal C_S\to\mathcal A_S$. On mapping objects its graph is $L(Q_S A(s,t))$, and $L(q_A(s,t))$ gives the coherent equivalence $V_S\eta_S\simeq U_\infty$.

source.place: Definition 5.1; cofibrant replacement and universal localization, with Kerodon 05ZP and 01DK.

proof.text:
For $P\in\mathcal D^{S^2}$ choose an objectwise cofibrant representative graph. Let $\alpha_P:G_S(P)\to\eta_S F_\infty(P)$ be the adjunct of $P\to U_\infty F_\infty(P)\simeq V_S\eta_S F_\infty(P)$. Both free graph formulas, in [lem-coef-fixed-object-dg-free-model] and [lem-coef-categorical-algebra-free-monad], have a summand for each path $s=x_0,\ldots,x_n=t$. The algebra formula has forward tensor order and the strict formula reverse order. The algebra theorem specifies the actual adjunct on a path: insert its edges as length-one generators and then compose. Step 2 therefore makes $V_S\alpha_P$ on this summand the map
$$a_1\otimes\cdots\otimes a_n\longmapsto(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}|a_i||a_j|}a_n\otimes\cdots\otimes a_1.$$
This is Koszul reversal; reversing twice gives sign $(-1)^{2\sum_{i<j}|a_i||a_j|}=1$. It is consequently a chain isomorphism on the path summand. For length zero it is the unit identification, and for length one the generating edge. By [lem-coef-projective-chains-monoidal-model] these tensors of cofibrant complexes compute the derived tensors. The two stated free formulas also identify their coproducts with those in $\mathcal D$. Thus the actual adjunct is a coproduct of equivalences at every pair $(s,t)$, and is an equivalence there. The units and adjuncts in the cited formulas are coherent and natural in $P$, so this is the canonical natural free comparison required below.

source.place: Proposition 5.2(f): explicit verification of the canonical free comparison.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-monadic-comparison] with $H=\eta_S$, $U=U_\infty$, $V=V_S$, $F=F_\infty$, $G=G_S$. Step 1 gives both left adjoints, conservativity of both graph functors, existence of all geometric realizations, and their preservation. Step 3 supplies the coherent equivalence $V_SH\simeq U_\infty$. Step 4 proves precisely that $V_S(\alpha_P)$, for the adjunct of the specified unit, is an equivalence for every $P$. These are every hypothesis of the comparison criterion; hence $\eta_S$ is an equivalence.

source.place: Final application in Proposition 5.2; Higher Algebra (2017), Corollary 4.7.3.16 and Remark 4.7.3.17.

proof.text: Restriction along $f:S\to T$ is the substitution $f^*A(s,t)=A(f(s),f(t))$. It preserves mappingwise quasi-isomorphisms and locally cofibrant objects. Thus the full relative categories $\mathbf C_S^{\rm lc}$ form a strict restriction diagram: $(gf)^*=f^*g^*$ on entries, units and compositions. Step 2 commutes with this diagram, including the Koszul reversals, since each operation is the same substituted chain map. Use the functorial localization of [lem-coef-simplicial-localization-existence] to localize the restriction diagrams. The functor-category universal property of these localizations, [def-coef-universally-localizing-simplicial-map] for the locally cofibrant relative categories and [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability] for the combinatorial model categories $\mathbf C_S$, descends the comparison and its diagrams of transformations, retaining all coherences. The inclusions $j_S$ form a natural map to the diagram of all dg categories and are equivalences after localization by Step 3. In the functor infinity category of these set-indexed diagrams, [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] makes this natural map an equivalence. Invert it there and compose with the localized Step 2 comparison. This gives a single coherent comparison on all dg categories; its evaluation at $S$ is the $Q_S$ comparison of Step 3. Identity and composition compatibility, including higher compatibility for longer strings of functions, belong to this one transformation and its inverse in the functor category. No assumption that $f^*$ preserves cofibrant dg categories is needed: local cofibrancy is preserved by its entry formula.

source.place: Definition 5.1, naturality in the object set; passage to Definition 5.3. Kerodon 05ZP and 01DK for the diagram argument.

proof.text: For $q_A:Q_SA\to A$, the mapping complex $Q_SA(s,t)$ is cofibrant and $q_A(s,t)$ is a quasi-isomorphism by [lem-coef-fixed-object-dg-free-model]. Step 3 assigns $L(Q_SA(s,t))$ as its mapping object. Localizing $q_A(s,t)$ identifies it with $L(A(s,t))$ by [lem-coef-projective-chains-monoidal-model]. For a strict dg functor $F:A\to B$, the square $q_B\,Q_SF=Fq_A$ commutes. Hence the map on mapping objects is the localized original chain map under these identifications. All these are transformations of actual functors and remain coherent under localization, as its universal property states in [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability]. Together with Step 6 this proves the stated functoriality for enriched functors and restriction maps.

source.place: Corollary 3.15, Definition 5.1; explicit evaluation of the natural replacement quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-algebroid-object-space-fibration], underlying arrows from $s$ to $t$ have mapping space $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(\mathbf Z[0],L(A(s,t)))$. By [lem-coef-projective-chains-monoidal-model], its components are chain maps $\mathbf Z[0]\to A(s,t)$ modulo chain homotopy, since $\mathbf Z[0]$ is cofibrant and every complex is fibrant. Such a map is determined by the degree-zero cycle $c=f(1)$; a degree-minus-one homotopy sends $1$ to some $b\in A(s,t)^{-1}$ and identifies $c,c'$ exactly when $c-c'=d(b)$. The quotient is $H^0A(s,t)$ by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a closed arrow in a noncofibrant $A$, lift its $H^0$ class to $Q_SA(s,t)$ using the quasi-isomorphism of Step 7, choose a cycle representative there, and use the just computed quotient; changing the representative by a boundary changes no component. Its image under $q_A$ has the original $H^0$ class, so it is precisely the prescribed underlying arrow. Units and composition are those of the dg category: after lifting two classes to $Q_SA$, its composition and the dg functor $q_A$ send their product to the original product. If $u'=u+db$ and $v'=v+de$ are degree-zero cycles with $b,e$ in degree $-1$, then $v'u'-vu=d(v'b+eu)$ by the chain-map Leibniz rule. Thus composition descends to those classes. Every dg functor preserves the cycles, boundaries and these products, giving the required naturality.

source.place: Definition 5.6 and Example 5.11; explicit chain-map, chain-homotopy and product calculations. The underlying mapping-space formula is supplied by lem-coef-algebroid-object-space-fibration, not by the definition of algebroids.
